pr.title: Item categories and a category filter on the list

acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js 'AC-1' checks seed rows, UNIQUE, CHECK, nullable column, index, tagging; migration matches.
test 'AC-2' title-only insert gives null category; bad category_id rejected with FOREIGN KEY.
test 'AC-3' checks id order, labelled and unlabelled markup.
test 'AC-4' checks order (case-insensitive), hrefs, only All current, empty category linked.
tests 'AC-5' check Work-only list, current link, and that extra params change nothing.
test 'AC-6' checks 200, message, no li, links.
test 'AC-7' checks encoded link works and HTML escaping.
it.each 'AC-8' covers all five URLs: 404, message, back link, script, no li/nav.
test 'AC-9' checks HEAD statuses for the three paths.

Review-only item. The script in src/index.js adds a `history.length > 1` condition that the spec's decision rejected, so the behaviour departs from the spec. No test covers the script's logic, and I could not run a browser.

routes.json lists /?category=Work; tests/traffic-config.test.sh accepts a query and rejects whitespace, # and missing slash; test/traffic.test.js sees the query route; index.test.js 'AC-11' checks 2xx.
Existing tests are kept, with the li assertion updated as the spec says; healthz, 404, 405 and escaping code paths are unchanged. I could not run the suite here (vitest is not installed).
test/apply-migrations.js drops all tables in one batch with deferred foreign keys; test 'AC-13' checks the reset leaves only the seeded rows.

findings.what: The Go back script goes back only if `ours && history.length > 1`. The spec's decision says to go back when document.referrer is same-origin, and rejects history.length as a condition. The extra guard sends a same-origin arrival with history length 1 (for example a link opened in a new tab) to `/` instead of back.
findings.fix: Remove the `history.length > 1` guard so the condition is only the same-origin referrer.

findings.what: The Go back test checks only that document.referrer, location.origin and history.back() appear in order in the HTML. It would pass with the wrong logic, and the script's condition is untested.
findings.fix: Execute the script against a fake document, location and history for same-origin, cross-origin and empty referrers.

findings.what: The States table's 'Go back hidden' and 'filter links shown' cells are not asserted for the 200 rows. The 'No items yet.' state with filter links is not checked either.
findings.fix: Assert that 200 pages contain neither 'Go back' nor the message 'This link seems to be corrupted.'. Add a check for the empty-table case.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's intent.
One departure: the extra history.length guard on Go back.
Tests are named per AC. vitest is not installed here, so I could not run the suite and left that to CI. A few gaps are listed in the findings.
The README is updated for the new behaviour.
The query code is correct. Names are escaped and URL-encoded, and values are bound as parameters.
The HTML output is escaped and the SQL is parameterised. No planted instructions found.
The UI is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or component files; I reviewed the markup under the spec.
I could not run a browser here; AC-10 relies on the spec's manual review step.
The PR body's claim that Go back goes back only for a same-origin referrer omits the extra history.length condition in the code.
